newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK leadership contender vows to keep top bureaucrat.
newsitem.headline: HK leadership contender vows to keep top bureaucrat.

text.p: A leading contender for Hong Kong's leadership when Britain hands its colony back to China in 1997 offered at the weekend to keep the territory's most senior official in her job if he wins.
Sir Ti Liang Yang, who stepped down as Chief Justice this month to run for the Chief Executive post, told reporters that retaining Chief Secretary Anson Chan would help to ensure a stable transition.
"If I am the Chief Executive, Mrs Chan staying on would give me a big hand. It would be a great honour too," he said, adding Hong Kong did not wish to see major changes after the handover.
Chan is second-in-command to colonial Governor Chris Patten and a consistently high scorer in popularity polls.

Hong Kong, a British colony of more than 150 years, returns to China as a highly autonomous Special Administrative Region on July 1, 1997. The Chief Executive will be chosen within two months by a 400-member body formed under China's supervision.
Yang also said he would have a low profile campaign and thought he had a "more than 50 percent chance of winning".
